coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 54
record.distance_note: On Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 30m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 waterfront lawn) -- versus roughly 470m from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50). Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay, not Mission Rock, on that basis. Pier 54 itself predates and is not part of Mission Bay's OCII development program -- it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure.

record.summary: Pier 54, a Port-owned pier on Terry A. Francois Blvd, was condemned and closed in 2024 after years of structural deterioration, displacing the businesses that operated there. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) budgets $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; no funded timeline exists yet for removing the rest of the structure.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a hand trace of the pier deck's visible outer edge on satellite imagery (accurate to a few metres at best), not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. It covers the deck and shed only, not the pilings or aprons beneath or beside it, and the pier's true outline under the shed roof cannot be seen. The Assessor's own outline for the pier is lot 9900054 (see digitized_from); this trace and that lot differ at the edges, with 92% of the trace inside the lot.
notes.digitized_from: Outline: a hand trace of the pier deck's outer edge on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29 per docs/satellite-imagery.md), read off a latitude/longitude grid and checked by overlay with the owner. No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available to trace from. Assessor lot: Pier 54 is lot 9900054 (block 9900, lot 054). DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset (acdm-wktn), queried by blklot on 2026-10-10, returns {"blklot":"9900054","block_num":"9900","lot_num":"054","active":true}, and its in_asr_secured_roll field reads true in the copy loaded 2026-10-01. Port piers carry no street name in that dataset, so a search for PIER-numbered street names finds none: they are block 9900, with the pier number as the lot. This hand trace lies 92% inside lot 9900054 and covers 89% of it; the lot outline has not been used in its place. The earlier placeholder box was anchored to the 500-599 Terry A. Francois Blvd address range (California State Parks Division of Boating and Waterways lists a combined 'Pier 54 & Pier 52 BLF' boat-launch facility on Terry A. Francois Blvd in this same stretch) and lay in open water south of the pier.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Pier 54 has its own Assessor lot, 9900054 (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, checked 2026-10-10). This record still draws a hand trace of the deck rather than that lot's outline.
notes.regulatory_context: Condemned and red-tagged in 2024; the Port announced it would permanently close at the end of 2024, displacing the pier's tenant businesses (SFGate, Sept 2024). The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31, Feb 2026) budgets a 'Pier 54 Shed Demolition' line item totaling $2.0M ($500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28); no line item for full substructure removal appears in that document.

open_questions: No funded plan yet for removing the pier's substructure beyond the shed demolition.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the closure-announcement milestone was dated December 2024, but the Port's August 9, 2024 memo says formal written notice went to tenants on July 15, 2024 and SFGate reported the closure in September 2024; it is now dated July 15, 2024. The February 2026 draft CIP milestone was flagged expected although the draft was published then; the flag was removed. Whether the shed demolition has started, and so whether 'being removed' is the right map status, is not confirmed: no source read says it has.

That the Port planned to fence the pier to prevent vandalism is reported only in a search-engine summary of the SFGate article, not independently re-verified here against the full original article text (which sits behind a paywall; the mirror used for this record's other facts may not repeat that detail).

This record's site grouping ("Mission Bay South") reflects DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area boundary, which reaches this stretch of Terry A. Francois Blvd -- not a claim that Pier 54 is a Mission Bay OCII development block, which it is not.

record.notes: This is a Port maritime/pier facility, not an OCII Mission Bay South development block -- grouped under the Mission Bay South site here because that is the nearest tracked site and because DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary for Mission Bay South extends north along the Terry A. Francois Blvd shoreline to include this stretch. It is materially farther from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50, ~470m away) than from Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 lawn, ~30m away). Recorded as adjacent rather than tracked because it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure being demolished, not a Mission Bay OCII development parcel like this site's other tracked records. A derelict timber pier stands just north of this footprint, separate from it (probably Pier 52, a separate Port asset; the identification is not confirmed by a source and it is not part of this record).
